notes:
Added

  • Hex travel — Fallout 1-style fast travel. Dragging the party token across a hex-gridded World Map scene is intercepted and replayed one hex at a time: each hex advances world time and rolls for a random encounter, and the journey halts where an encounter fires.
    • Party actor — the fallout system has no group actor type, so the module creates one on request (an npc with real health, owned by all players, never a 0 HP character in the directory) and selects it as the map's token. Its roster records who is travelling.
    • Encounters — chance per hex, reduced by the party's best Survival rank (the Outdoorsman analogue) down to a configurable floor. Tables are a world default, overridable per terrain by a table picker added to Region configs.
    • Pace — a Seconds per Hex setting drives the whole journey: the token's glide, the counter's spin, and the clock all derive from it, so nothing drifts out of step. The party walks the route rather than teleporting.
    • The Wayfarer — encounter checks are shown as a Vault-Tec counter with three mechanical number reels that spin up and settle left to right, in place of dice. It reports the target, the result, and CLEAR or ENCOUNTER.
    • Every roll is recorded — the journey's chat card lists each hex's roll against the chance, so a quiet crossing is as legible as an eventful one.
    • Time — advanced once per hex as it is crossed, through Calendaria's own advanceTime API when present and core game.time otherwise, so Simple Calendar and Seasons & Stars follow along without a dependency.

Full details in the release notes.
